trust_decision.summary: In HTTP mode, ApiKeyMiddleware decides whether a request may run tools; when no client key is supplied it forwards the request anyway and the client layer falls back to the ContextVar default, which is the server's NETLICENSING_API_KEY env var.

landing_point.why: The summary names HTTP mode and the server-side key; the only HTTP-specific auth code is the ApiKeyMiddleware nested in main(), and its final line forwards keyless requests.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP POST/GET /mcp (streamable-http app built at src/netlicensing_mcp/server.py:2042-2043), started via `netlicensing-mcp http`

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The fix only rewrites ApiKeyMiddleware (moved to module level, fix.diff:361-390, old body removed fix.diff:400-420). The safety.py and other server.py hunks (fix.diff:217-356) only reformat lines.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the O8 route: the solver can argue that only `netlicensing-mcp http` (main()) is the supported HTTP deployment, and that running server.py through the FastMCP CLI or another FastMCP transport is an unsupported, operator-chosen setup.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Two things must keep working: (1) /health stays unauthenticated for load-balancer probes, and (2) stdio mode keeps using the NETLICENSING_API_KEY env default. A fix that blanket-rejects every path, or that removes the env-var default in client.py, breaks one of them.

O6_input_shapes: empty or whitespace-only x-netlicensing-api-key, now stripped (fix.diff:368)
Authorization: Bearer with empty or whitespace-only token, now stripped (fix.diff:370-372)
?apikey= query parameter, no longer accepted as a key source (removed at fix.diff:411-412)

O7_producer.where: src/netlicensing_mcp/client.py:29-31 (ContextVar default read from os.getenv at import time, after load_dotenv at client.py:21)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: When server.py is served through FastMCP's own HTTP transports (mcp.run / `mcp run` with streamable-http or sse), the app is built without ApiKeyMiddleware, so keyless requests still fall back to the env key; the published fix still attaches the middleware only inside main().
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The documented HTTP entry is `netlicensing-mcp http` (server.py:8, Dockerfile:37, deploy/aws/ecs-fargate.yaml:294). The FastMCP CLI path appears only as `mcp dev` for the Inspector (server.py:9).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, different mechanism (third-party FastMCP app factory rather than project code)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second custom_route (for example a /status or /metrics endpoint) that calls nl_get through the env-key ContextVar and is exempted like /health.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The health route is already exempted by path, and a maintainer adding an ops endpoint that reports account or API status would naturally exempt it the same way.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An SSE app (mcp.sse_app()) mounted next to the streamable-http app for legacy MCP clients, without the middleware.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Many FastMCP servers offer SSE alongside streamable-http for older clients; mounting a second Starlette app is a one-line addition.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second key source in client._headers (for example a per-tool api_key argument, or a fallback to os.environ when the ContextVar is empty).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The header builder already contains a fallback chain (env default, then demo:demo); adding one more fallback is a natural convenience change and reintroduces the server-key use without touching the middleware.

O9_family: missing authentication for a critical function / fallback to ambient server credentials (CWE-306)

O10_build.toolchain: pip/hatch (hatch-vcs), pytest with asyncio_mode=auto, starlette TestClient
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_tools.py and tests/test_safety_tokens.py mock nl_get/nl_post; at the pinned commit no test covers the HTTP middleware (the fix adds tests/test_auth_middleware.py).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Return 401 in the existing nested middleware when the key is missing, leaving empty or whitespace keys and the query-param source as they are and keeping the middleware attached only in main().

out_of_scope_notes: deploy/aws/README.md:116-136 documents passing the API key in the ?apikey= query string (the key ends up in access logs); the fix removes this source but the doc is not changed.
src/netlicensing_mcp/client.py:66-67 falls back to shared demo:demo credentials when no key is set.
unverified: The O8 route depends on how the FastMCP SDK builds its streamable-http/sse apps under mcp.run or `mcp run`; SDK code was not read, so it is not confirmed that no middleware applies there.

Not checked: whether the ContextVar set in the middleware reaches tool calls that run in the streamable-http session task, which may have been created under an earlier request's context. That is a possible how-type issue on key identity across requests.
